subject.title: [security] Manage-share run events can reattribute runs into another lease's audit history

question: Should manage-share recipients be allowed to add owner-readable run audit attribution to a shared lease through post-create run events, or should that be limited to the lease owner/admin or a validated replacement flow?
rationale: Current docs and VISION.md push against silent retargeting of ownership claims, but the recent related maintainer discussion accepted manage access as the guard, so automation should not choose the permanent authorization contract.

options.title: Block event-only manage reattribution
options.body: Reject or ignore manage-share event lease IDs unless the run already belongs to that lease or a server-validated replacement flow proves the backing lease relationship.

options.title: Confirm manage-share as trusted
options.body: Document that manage-share recipients may create owner-readable audit attribution through run events and close this as accepted behavior after maintainer sign-off.

options.title: Add a dedicated attach path
options.body: Keep ordinary events from expanding attribution and add a narrow API for post-create lease attachment with explicit validation and tests.

recommendation.title: Block event-only manage reattribution
recommendation.body: Reject or ignore manage-share event lease IDs unless the run already belongs to that lease or a server-validated replacement flow proves the backing lease relationship.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the shared-lease audit model and made the related expected-behavior call, so they are the best available owner for the contract decision.
